question_text: A fish vendor bought fish for P800 and sold it for P1,040. What is the percentage profit?

hint_ladder.title: Find the Profit First
hint_ladder.text: Alamin muna ang kinita: Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price. Dito: P1,040 - P800 = P240.

hint_ladder.title: The Key Formula
hint_ladder.text: Formula: (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100%. Ang cost ang base—dito P800. Tandaan, puhunan ang base, hindi selling price.

hint_ladder.title: Plug in the Numbers
hint_ladder.text: Ilagay sa formula: (P240 ÷ P800) × 100%. I-simplify: 240/800 = 0.3. Multiply by 100% para makuha ang percent.

hint_ladder.title: Almost There
hint_ladder.text: 0.3 times 100% equal 30%. Kaya 30% ang profit. Perfect!

A.text: You might have chosen A because you divided profit by selling price (P240/P1,040≈23%, rounded to 25%).

C.text: You might have chosen C because of a division slip, thinking 240/800 is 0.35 instead of 0.3.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you used an incorrect cost (P600), giving 240/600=0.4.

next_time_rule: Profit % always uses cost as denominator: (Profit / Cost) x 100%. Huwag gamitin ang selling price — cost ang base.
deconstruct_text:
Sa palengke ni Aling Nena, bumili siya ng bangus sa halagang P800 at binenta ng P1,040. Una, kunin ang kita: P1,040 - P800 = P240.

Pagkatapos, ang formula ng percentage profit: (Kita ÷ Puhunan) × 100%. I-divide mo ang P240 sa P800, equals 0.3, times 100% = 30%. Mental trick: 'Kita over Puhunan' — laging puhunan ang base, huwag selling price.

**Watch-Out Zone: wrong_base_percentage** in action. Selling price mali; cost ang base.
